localContext: Many Berwyn homes feature Chicago-style brick bungalows from the 1920s. These properties often include original detached alley garages. The hardware in these garages can be 100 years old. These systems were built for narrower Model T-era vehicles. Modern SUVs often strain these older garage doors and components. Lift cables wear down under this increased demand. Chicagoland’s cold winters and humid summers also stress metal parts. Cables can fray, rust, or snap. We see this often in garages near the Depot District and the Proksa Park area. Old cables on original drums are not designed for today's wider, heavier vehicles or daily use. Our repair targets these specific issues for Berwyn residents.

problemSigns.detail: Your garage door may sag on one side in the opening. This indicates uneven lifting force, likely due to a cable issue.

problemSigns.sign: Cable loose or wrapped off drum
problemSigns.detail: You may see a cable hanging freely or tangled around the cable drum above the door. This means it is not operating correctly.
A harsh grinding sound when the door moves can signal a cable rubbing or improperly seated on the drum.
If the door drops quickly or with excessive force, a cable may have broken, removing the spring tension on one side.

process.description: Our technician arrives, inspects your garage door cables and related hardware. You receive an upfront, flat-rate quote before any work starts.
We replace worn or broken cables with new galvanized aircraft-grade lift cables. We also replace cable drums or bottom brackets if needed. Our trucks stock common parts.
We adjust the door's tension and alignment. This ensures smooth and balanced operation.
After repair, we perform a balance test and a safety-reverse test. This confirms your garage door works correctly and safely.
